patch.value: The relationship lexicon cannot express recurrence, so a defect family fixed thirty times is thirty unrelated nodes to every graph algorithm

Verified live 2026-08-03 by asking the product to accept the relation and reading its refusal.

The accepted dependency-kind domain is fifteen spellings: blocks, parent, child, parent_child, child_of, related, related_to, discovered_from, blocked_by, incident_from, epic, implements, supersedes, task, verifies. None of them means "this is the same defect again". The closest candidates are all something else. supersedes means replacement, and the replaced thing is expected to stop existing; a recurrence does not supersede its predecessor, because the predecessor was correctly fixed. discovered_from means derivation of knowledge, not repetition of a failure. incident_from means an item was raised from an incident and carries three rows in the entire corpus. related is undirected and carries no semantics at all.

The measured consequence is severe. A defect family that has been diagnosed and fixed roughly thirty times over eight months exists in the graph as roughly thirty disconnected items. Graph traversal cannot reach the second occurrence from the first. Ancestors, descendants, impact, dominators, centrality and community detection all see thirty independent defects. Every analytic the project has built for understanding its own history is blind to the single most expensive pattern in that history.

There is a live conformance gap. A feature filed the same day specifies a recurrence analyzer whose acceptance criteria require it to fold "typed recurrence or supersedes edges" into versioned defect families. Typed recurrence edges cannot be written. The feature therefore cannot be satisfied without either extending the lexicon or silently reinterpreting supersedes, and reinterpreting supersedes would corrupt the fifty-seven existing rows that mean replacement.

The gap is a missing relation, not a missing canonicalization and not a missing promotion pass. The lexicon item owns collapsing fifteen spellings onto one canonical spelling per relation, and must land first so that a new relation is added to a governed vocabulary rather than a sixteenth ungoverned spelling. The lineage item owns promoting evolution statements that already exist in durable text onto the kinds that already exist. Neither creates a relation that does not exist, and neither can, because the promotion rule has no target kind to promote recurrence into.

Recurrence also needs semantics the existing kinds do not carry: it is directional and time-ordered, it must survive the closure of both endpoints, it must be assertable between items with different root causes but the same observable failure, and it must be distinguishable from a duplicate. A duplicate says two records describe one event. A recurrence says two events share an identity.

A recurrence relation exists in the declared dependency-kind domain with stated direction, time ordering, and terminal-endpoint validity, and is distinguishable from supersedes and from duplicate; The relation is added to the canonical vocabulary rather than as a sixteenth ungoverned spelling, so the lexicon consolidation lands first and the new kind is defined against the consolidated set; Graph traversal, impact, dominators and community detection reach every occurrence of a family from any other occurrence, proved on the historical platform-regression family; The existing supersedes rows keep replacement semantics unchanged and no row is retyped by the introduction of the new relation; The recurrence analyzer feature can satisfy its typed-recurrence acceptance criterion without reinterpreting any existing kind

value.text:
Independent confirmation found the same day this item was filed, from the project's own governance output rather than from reasoning about the lexicon.

The metadata validator now reports two duplicate issue codes, not one. The long-standing pair is GH-209 on pm-1byt and pm-25se, two genuinely distinct defects a release apart. The second pair is GH-779 on pm-ajaskl, closed 2026-07-28, and pm-wnbk2l, closed 2026-08-02. The second item is titled with the literal word recurrence.

That pair is the argument in miniature. Someone needed to state that a fixed defect had returned. No kind exists for it, so the recurrence was encoded twice over in places that were never meant to carry it: once in the title, by reusing the upstream issue code as a prefix, and once in the graph as discovered_from, which asserts derivation of knowledge and not repetition of a failure. The item does carry discovered_from to its predecessor, so the author reached for the nearest available kind and it was the wrong one.

Then the governance layer read the workaround and called it a defect. A duplicate issue code is exactly what the title-namespace workaround produces, so the only surface in the project that noticed the recurrence reported it as a data-quality error and proposed renaming or merging the two items. Renaming would erase the only recorded trace of the recurrence. Merging would destroy one of two correctly closed items.

Two facts follow. The need is real and has now arisen at least twice through independent authors. And the absence is actively harmful rather than merely missing, because the substitute encodings are indistinguishable from mistakes and the tooling treats them as such.

Recorded as evidence on this item. The duplicate-code check itself keeps its existing owner and its existing check-side disposition, and neither pair should be renamed or merged.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Measured recurrence family, 2026-08-16 — "the check enumerates a set it maintains instead of the set the artifact defines". Scanned all 1,547 Issue and Task items, open and terminal.

Seven instances, six already fixed and one found today:

  pm-b84irw   closed   Measure source replication against an independently discovered denominator
  pm-te6elw   closed   SDK completeness asserted by a 10-case curated array against 85 declared actions
  pm-1jrdri   closed   The rendered command surface is not a subset of the contracted surface
  pm-6j7r1a   closed   The runtime contract enumeration is not closed over the surface it can resolve
  pm-xpumg4   closed   The boundary gate proves the CLI stopped importing private core and never proves it only imports the published SDK
  pm-7wx1f9   closed   Nested workspace snapshot and help paths are enumerated but not resolvable
  pm-suhxny   open     The public-surface gate enumerates its own hand-written entrypoint list; two published code exports ship ungoverned

Every one of them has the same three-part shape. A machine-readable artifact defines a set to the outside world — the export map, the workflow files, the command registration, the action table. A checker keeps its own enumeration of that set. The checker proves its list against the artifact and never proves the artifact against its list, so the check is complete over its own belief and silent about everything the artifact gained since the belief was written.

Two properties make this family worth detecting specifically rather than treating each instance as a one-off.

It fails open and it fails silently. Every one of the seven passed green while the gap existed. The failure is not a wrong answer, it is a correct answer to a smaller question, which is invisible in a pass/fail verdict and only appears when someone computes the denominator independently.

It recurs at the moment of growth. Nothing breaks when the hand list is written; the divergence begins the first time the artifact gains an entry. So the defect is introduced by a change that is unrelated to the checker, by an author who has no reason to look at it, which is precisely the situation review does not catch.

## The detectable signature

For pm-1qkivy this family is a concrete first target, because the signature is narrow enough to detect without drowning in false positives:

- a module under scripts/ or src/ that declares a frozen literal collection (Object.freeze over an object or array, or a `new Set([...])` of string literals), and
- reads a structured artifact in the same function or module — package.json, a workflows directory, a generated contract table, a registry JSON — and
- indexes into the artifact using members of the literal, rather than iterating the artifact.

That third clause is the discriminator. `for (const key of MY_LIST) lookup(artifact[key])` is the defect; `for (const key of Object.keys(artifact)) require(MY_MAP[key])` is the correct shape.

## The positive control already in the repository

scripts/release/gate-registry.mjs implements the correct shape. `discoverWorkflowGates` parses every file under .github/workflows and returns the real job identifiers, then `validateGateRegistry` checks both directions explicitly: `pipeline:<id>:unregistered` when the artifact has an entry the registry lacks, and `pipeline:<id>:not_enforced` when the registry has an entry the artifact lacks. The hand-maintained registry is annotation on a derived set, never the enumeration.

That gives any detector a same-repository positive control and a same-repository negative control, which is what pm-rtn5h6's escape ratchet asks every new gate to carry. It also means the fix for each instance is a known refactor rather than a design question.

## Cost of the escapes

Six shipped fixes for one shape. The seventh escaped into a published artifact: 2026.8.16 on npm resolves `@unbrained/pm-cli/cli` to a declaration file exporting 86 internal helpers, and the surface gate that exists to prevent exactly that reported "0 classified changes" for it. Installing the published tarball with bun and importing the entrypoint returns both symbols, typed.

Recorded on pm-1qkivy as a detector target and on pm-ouyq3n as a worked example of a recurrence the current relationship lexicon cannot express: these seven items are seven unrelated nodes to any graph walk, and the only thing tying them together today is this note.
